summary: Michael Willis specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Victoria and under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Pramod Chandra at the University of Chicago (PhD 1988), later serving as British Museum curator (1994–2014).

Michael Witzel is an Indologist and linguist who studied under scholars including Paul Thieme, Karl Hoffmann, and F. B. J. Kuiper. He directed the Nepal Research Centre (1972–1978) and held Sanskrit chairs at Leiden (1978–1986) and Harvard (1986, 2022).

Michael Zimmermann is an expert in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Hamburg (PhD) and Soka University under Lambert Schmithausen and others, he held posts at Stanford, directed the Nepal Research Centre (2002), and became professor at Hamburg.

Michael von Brück works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Rostock (1968–1973) and held professorships at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and the University of Munich (~1991–2014).

Michaela Haas is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed her PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2008) under the supervision of Peter Schwieger, and also studied with Rechungpa and Jigme Namgyal Dzigar Kongtrul.

Michaela Mross specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Komazawa University and completed her PhD at the University of Munich (2014) before teaching as a Japanese Buddhism professor at Stanford University (attested 2017, 2026).

Michel Bitbol works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Paris Diderot University and under Pierre Mills, he has held posts as research director at CNRS (~1990) and affiliations with Linacre College, Oxford, and École Normale Supérieure.

Michel Bréal was a linguist and Indologist who studied at École Normale Supérieure and under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He served as professor at the Collège de France (1864–1905) and director at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1882).

Michel Hulin was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and Paris-Sorbonne University under Olivier Lacombe, later teaching at Paris-Sorbonne University from 1981 to 1998.
Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Jean Boisselier (1988) and served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1989–2003).
Michel Leiris studied at Lycée Janson-de-Sailly (~1916–1918) and under Marcel Mauss (~1929–1931).

Michel Lejeune was a linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Antoine Meillet (~1926–1929). He held academic posts at the University of Poitiers (~1937–1941), the University of Paris (~1951–1955), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1951–1978).

Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied under Seizan Yanagida and earned his PhD at the University of Geneva, later holding posts at Hanazono University (attested 2000–2006) and the University of Hawaiʻi.

Michel Soymié was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at INALCO. He held posts at CNRS, EFEO, and held the Chair of History and Philosophy of Mediaeval China at EPHE (~1966–1992).

Michel Strickmann was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University under Max Kaltenmark and Kristofer Schipper, later serving as an assistant professor at UC Berkeley (1978).

Michela Clemente is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015), and held a Marie Sklodowska Curie Fellowship at the University of Cambridge.

Michele Kerbaker was an Italian Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin under Giacomo Lignana. He taught Sanskrit at University of Naples 'L'Orientale' (1870) and philology at the University of Naples Federico II (~1876–1914).
Michele Martin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and held a post at National Taiwan University.

Michelle Spuler is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Queensland (~1996–2001) and taught at Colorado College and Victoria University of Wellington (~2002–2004).

Michiel de Vaan is a linguist and Iranian/Central Asian studies specialist. He completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky (~1998–2002) and held an academic post at Leiden University (~2003–2014).
